Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 1:

﴿They ask you about the spoils (al-anfal).﴾ To whom do the spoils belong? It was revealed concerning the spoils of Badr, and they differed about them. The young men (al-shubban) said: "They belong to us, because we engaged in the fighting." The elders (al-ashyakh) said: "We were a reserve (radan) for you, because we stood in the battle lines with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Had you been routed, you would have retreated to us, so do not take the spoils without us." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger.﴾ He places them wherever He wills, without anyone sharing in them. So he divided them among them equally (ʿala al-sawaʾ). ﴿So fear Allah﴾ by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience, ﴿and set right the matter between you﴾ — truly, your bonds of connection (wasl) — that is: do not oppose one another. ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ — submit to them regarding the spoils, for they judge concerning them as they wish. ﴿If you are believers.﴾ Then he described the believers, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾. That is: the believer is one who, when Allah is made a cause of fear, his heart is struck with dread and he submits to His command. ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith﴾, meaning in assent and certainty. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾, meaning they place their trust in Allah, hoping for nothing other than Him.

These are the true believers, in truth, without doubt, unlike the faith of the hypocrites. ﴿For them there are ranks with their Lord﴾, meaning: ranks of Paradise, ﴿and forgiveness and a generous provision﴾, and this is the provision of Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 5:

﴿As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾: that is, proceed with the command of Allah concerning the spoils, even though some of them dislike it, because the young men wanted to take it for themselves. So Allah the Exalted said: give to whomever You wish, even if they dislike it, just as you went forth in obedience to the command of Allah to set out, while they were averse to it. The meaning of ﴿as your Lord brought you out of your house﴾ is: He commanded you to set out from Madinah toward the caravan of Quraysh ﴿in truth﴾: by the revelation that Jibril brought you. ﴿And indeed, a group of the believers were averse﴾: to going out with you, a natural aversion because of the hardship they anticipated, for they knew that they would not capture the caravan without fighting.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 6:

﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾ — concerning the fighting, after they had been commanded to it. The reason was that they went out for the caravan (al-ʿIr) and had not taken up the equipment of war. When they were commanded to fight the army (al-Nafir), it weighed heavily on them, and they sought permission to avoid it; this was their disputing.

﴿As if they were being driven to death while they look on﴾ — that is, because of their intense aversion to meeting the people, it was as if they were being driven to death with their own eyes witnessing it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 7:

﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours,﴾ namely the caravan or the army (al-nafir). ﴿And you wished that the one without thorns (armed force) would be yours.﴾ That is, the caravan, which had no weapons, would be yours. ﴿But Allah intends to establish the truth﴾ He makes it manifest and exalted ﴿by His words﴾ by His promises, which preceded the manifestation of Islam ﴿and to cut off the last remnant of the disbelievers﴾ that is, He commanded you to fight Quraysh only for this purpose.

Surah al-Anfal (8), verse 8, in al-Wahidi's Commentary (al-Wajiz):

﴿That He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood, even though the criminals disliked it.﴾ Meaning: and He cuts off the last remnant of the disbelievers, so that He may make the truth manifest and exalted, and nullify falsehood, and destroy disbelief and bring it to an end, even though the criminals dislike that.

﴿When you sought help from your Lord﴾, asking Him for forgiveness through victory over the enemy, because of your small number. ﴿So He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another"﴾ — ﴿mardifin﴾, meaning in succession. They came after the Muslims. Whoever reads ﴿mudhdhifin﴾ with a fatha on the dal (مَرْدَفِين) means: God caused the Muslims to be followed by a thousand of them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 10:

﴿And Allah did not make it﴾, i.e., the reinforcement, ﴿except as good news﴾. The verse has already passed in Surah Al 'Imran.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 11:

﴿When He overcame you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾ This is because Allah, exalted is He, gave them a security, and drowsiness overtook them while with Him. This was as it was on the day of Uhud, and we have mentioned that in Surat Al 'Imran. ﴿And He sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby﴾ This is because, when they were encamped against the polytheists at Badr, a group of them became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity requiring a full washing). The polytheists had got to the water before them, and Satan whispered to them and said: "How can you hope for victory when they have overcome you at the water, while you pray in a state of major impurity and minor impurity, and you claim that you are the friends of Allah, and His Prophet is among you?" So Allah, exalted is He, sent down rain, from which the valley flowed, until they washed themselves and the whispering departed. This is His saying: ﴿to purify you thereby﴾, that is: from minor and major impurities. ﴿And remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾, his whispering, which earns the punishment of Allah. ﴿And to strengthen upon your hearts﴾ with certainty and victory. ﴿And plant firmly thereby the feet﴾. This is because they had descended upon a sand dune in which their feet sank, so the rain packed it down until the feet became firm upon it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 12:

﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels: "I am with you; so strengthen those who believe."﴾ Those whom He sent to the Muslims. ﴿I am with you﴾ with help and support. ﴿So strengthen those who believe﴾ by giving them the good news of victory. The angel was in front of the line in the form of a man, saying: "Rejoice, for Allah is your helper." ﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾ fear of My friends. ﴿So strike above the necks﴾ meaning: the heads. ﴿And strike every fingertip of them﴾ meaning: the extremities of the hands and feet.

The Qur'anic quotation: ﴿That﴾ — the striking (the punishment) — ﴿because they opposed God and His Messenger﴾ — they separated themselves from them both and opposed them.

Wait, I need to correct that: the translation should be as follows.

﴿That﴾ the striking (al-darb) ﴿because they opposed (shaqqu) God and His Messenger﴾ — they separated from them both and went against them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 14:

﴿That﴾ refers to the killing and striking at Badr. ﴿So taste it, and indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire﴾ — after what befell them of having their necks struck.

O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing [in a mass] (zahfan), (meaning) gathered together and drawing near to you for battle, ﴿then do not turn your backs to them﴾, (meaning) do not make your backs face toward them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 16:

﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day﴾, i.e., the day of meeting the disbelievers, ﴿turning his back, except as a stratagem for battle﴾, one who swerves aside, withdrawing in order to return, ﴿or retreating to a company﴾, one who joins himself ﴿to a group﴾, a host, intending to return to the fighting, ﴿then he has incurred wrath from Allah﴾, to the end of the verse. Most of the exegetes hold that this threat was only for those who fled on the day of Badr, and that this ruling was specific to those who were routed on the day of Badr.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 17:

﴿So you did not kill them﴾, meaning: on the day of Badr. ﴿But it was Allah who killed them﴾, through His causing that by way of the aid against them and the strengthening of hearts. ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾. The reason for this is that Jibril (peace be upon him) said to the Prophet (peace be upon him) on the day of Badr: "Take a handful of dust and throw it at them." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a handful of pebbles from the valley and threw them at the faces of the people, and no polytheist remained without some of it entering his eyes, and that was the cause of their defeat. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but Allah threw﴾. That is: a handful of pebbles does not fill the eyes of that large army when thrown by a human being, but Allah the Exalted undertook to deliver it into their sight. ﴿And that He might test the believers with a good trial from Him﴾, and bestow upon them a great blessing by victory and booty; He did that. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾ of their supplication, ﴿Knowing﴾ of their intentions.

﴿That is so, and [know that] Allah weakens the plot of the disbelievers.﴾ He congratulates His Messenger (ﷺ) on weakening the plot of his enemy, until their tyrants were killed and their nobles were taken prisoner.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 19:

﴿If you seek a victory,﴾ this is addressed to the polytheists, for Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: "O Allah, grant victory to the better of the two religions and the more guided of the two groups." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you seek a victory,﴾ you seek victory for the more guided of the two groups. ﴿Then there has certainly come to you the victory,﴾ that is, the triumph. ﴿And if you cease,﴾ from polytheism with Allah, ﴿it is better for you; but if you return,﴾ to fighting Muhammad, ﴿We will return,﴾ against you with killing and capture. ﴿And your company will not avail you at all,﴾ that is, will not repel from you, ﴿your company,﴾ your group, ﴿anything, even if it is great﴾ in number. ﴿And that Allah is with the believers,﴾ so the victory is theirs.

O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him, while you are hearing [the Qur'an].

Do not turn away from him by opposing his command, while you are hearing what has been revealed of the Qur'an.

Translation:

﴿And do not be like those who say, "We hear,"﴾ while they do not hear [in the sense of receptive hearing]. He means the hypocrites. It has also been said: He means the polytheists, because they heard but did not reflect upon what they heard, so they were in the position of one who had not heard.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 22:

﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the dumb who do not use reason.﴾ He means a group of the polytheists who were deaf to the truth, so they do not hear it, and dumb in speaking it. Allah the Exalted has made clear that these are the worst of the creatures that crawl upon the earth.

﴿Had Allah known any good in them﴾, [meaning], had He known that they would be made righteous by the proofs and signs He presents to them, ﴿He would have made them hear﴾ them with the hearing of understanding. ﴿And even if He had made them hear﴾ after He had known that there is no good in them, they would not have benefited from it, and ﴿they would have turned away while they were averse﴾.

O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. Answer them both with obedience. (Verse 24 of Surah al-Anfal.)

That which gives you life means: because through it their affair is given life and strengthened; and because it is the cause of martyrdom, and the martyrs are alive with their Lord; and because it is the cause of everlasting life in Paradise.

And know that Allah comes between a man and his heart: Allah comes between a person and his heart, so that he cannot believe except by His permission, nor disbelieve. The hearts are in the hand of Allah, the Exalted; He turns them however He wills.

And that to Him you will be gathered: for the recompense for deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 25:

﴿And guard against a trial that will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾ The verse: Allah the Exalted commands the believers not to allow wrongdoing (al-munkar) to persist among them, lest Allah encompass them all with punishment and trial. The trial here is: allowing wrongdoing to persist and not changing it. His words ﴿will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong﴾ mean: it will strike the wrongdoer and the wronged alike, and will not be confined to the wrongdoers alone; rather it is general. The sense is: "Guard against a trial, for if you do not guard against it, it will not afflict only those among you who have done wrong"; that is, it will not fall only upon the wrongdoers to the exclusion of others, but it will fall upon the righteous and the wicked alike. ﴿And know that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ This is an exhortation to adhere to uprightness out of fear of the trial and of Allah's punishment for disobedience committed within it.

"And remember" — [addressing] the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun), ﴿when you were few﴾, meaning: when they were in Makkah at the beginning of Islam, before they numbered forty; ﴿oppressed in the land﴾, meaning: the land of Makkah; ﴿fearing that the people would snatch you away﴾, meaning: the polytheists among the Arabs, if you went out from it; ﴿so He sheltered you﴾, meaning: He made for you a refuge to which you could return, and joined you to the Helpers (al-Ansar); ﴿and strengthened you with His help﴾, meaning: on the day of Badr, with the angels; ﴿and provided you with good things﴾, meaning: the spoils of war, which He made lawful for you; ﴿that you may be grateful﴾, meaning: so that you obey.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 27:

﴿O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger⁠—by abandoning His obligations⁠—﴾ and by abandoning his sunnah, ﴿and do not betray your trusts﴾, meaning: and do not betray your trusts, ﴿while you know﴾ that they are trusts without any doubt. Each of the trusts that Allah has entrusted to His servants is a trust, and every person is entrusted with what Allah has made obligatory upon him.

It is said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him to the Banu Qurayzah when he besieged them, and his family and children were among them. They said to him: "What do you advise us? Should we submit to the judgment of Sa'd concerning us?" Abu Lubabah gestured toward his throat, meaning that it would be slaughter, so do not do it. And this was a betrayal of Allah and His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 28:

﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ i.e., a test through which what is in the soul becomes manifest, whether it follows its desires or avoids them. For this reason Abu Lubaba inclined toward Qurayza when he disclosed to them the judgment of Sa'd, because his wealth and his children were among them. ﴿And indeed, with Allah is a great reward﴾ for the one who fulfills the trust and does not betray it.

O you who have believed, if you fear Allah [by avoiding betrayal in what has been mentioned], He will grant you a criterion (furqan) [that distinguishes you from what you fear, so you are saved], and He will remove from you your misdeeds [He will erase from you the sins that have passed], and Allah is the Owner of great bounty [He does not withhold from you what He has promised you for obedience to Him].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 30:

﴿And when those who disbelieve plot against you﴾ This was because the polytheists of Quraysh conspired together in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of Quraysh) concerning Muhammad (ﷺ). Some of them said: "Confine him, and let us wait for him until the fate of death (ریب المنون) overtakes him." Others said: "Expel him from among you, and you will be rid of his harm." Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him, said: "This is not the right opinion. Rather, kill him by having one man from every clan gather around him and strike him with the blow of a single man. When they have killed him, his blood will be scattered among the tribes, and the Banu Hashim will not be able to fight all of Quraysh." So Allah the Exalted revealed to His Prophet what they were planning and commanded him to emigrate (hijrah). This is His saying:

﴿to confine you﴾, meaning: to bind you and shackle you. ﴿Or kill you﴾ all of them together, in the manner of one man's killing, as the accursed Abu Jahl said. ﴿Or expel you﴾ from Makkah to some remote part of the earth. ﴿And they plot, and Allah plots﴾, meaning: He will repay them for the fitting consequence of their plotting by granting victory to the believers over them. ﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾, the best of those who repay, with the evil of punishment for their evil. This is because He destroyed those who plotted against His Prophet and delivered him from them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 31:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾ — the verse. Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith had gone out to al-Hirah as a merchant and bought the tales of Kalilah wa Dimnah. He would sit with the mockers and recite them to them. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related the account of the earlier generations, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith said: "If I wished, I could say the like of this. This is nothing but what the ancients wrote down in their books." And al-Nadr also said:

"O Allah, if this (that Muhammad says) is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, as You rained them upon the people of Lut, or bring us a painful punishment." That is: with some of the punishments with which the nations were punished. The intensity of his enmity toward the Prophet ﷺ led him to utter such a statement, in order to give the impression that he was certain of his matter and in complete confidence that Muhammad's cause was not the truth.

Qur'anic quotations in ﴿ ﴾ are kept with translated meaning.

﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾. And Allah would not punish the polytheists while you were residing among them, because Allah never punished a town until the Prophet and those who believed with him had gone out from it. ﴿And Allah would not be punishing them﴾ — these disbelievers — while among them were believers, ﴿and they seek forgiveness﴾ — meaning: the Muslims. Then he said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 34:

﴿And what [excuse] do they have that Allah should not punish them,﴾ i.e., and why would Allah not punish them with the sword after the departure of those he meant by His words: ﴿while they seek forgiveness?﴾ from among them. ﴿And they bar⁠ [people] from the Sacred Mosque⁠﴾ they prevent the Prophet and the believers ﴿from the Sacred Mosque﴾ from circumambulating it. ﴿Yet they are not its guardians.⁠﴾ That is because they said: "We are the guardians of the Mosque." So Allah refuted them with His words: ﴿Its guardians are none but the righteous⁠﴾ meaning: the Emigrants (muhajirun) and the Helpers (ansar). ﴿But most of them do not know⁠﴾ the unseen knowledge of Mine and what has preceded in My decree.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 35:

﴿Their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping.﴾ That is: whistling (ṣafīr) and clapping (taṣfīq). The Quraysh used to circumambulate the House naked, whistling and clapping. They made this their prayer, so their drawing near to God was by whistling and clapping. ﴿So taste the punishment﴾ at Badr ﴿for what you used to disbelieve﴾, that is, deny the Oneness of God, exalted is He.

Indeed, those who disbelieve ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ — it was revealed concerning those who spent on the war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the days of Badr, and they were twelve men. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then they will spend it, and then it will become a regret for them﴾ through the loss of the wealth and the failure of their aim.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 37:

﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good﴾ i.e., you will be gathered into Jahannam so that He may distinguish between the people of wretchedness and the people of happiness. ﴿And put the wicked, one part of it upon another﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, and it is a collective noun (ism al-jins), ﴿one part of it upon another﴾ joins some of them to others; ﴿and heap them all together﴾ i.e., gathers them until it becomes like a heaped-up cloud; then ﴿He puts them into Hell. Those are the losers﴾ because they exchanged their wealth for the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 38:

﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾, Abu Sufyan and his companions: ﴿if they desist﴾ from polytheism and fighting the believers, ﴿their past will be forgiven﴾, what has preceded of fornication and polytheism, because the one at war (ḥarbī), when he embraces Islam, returns like the day his mother bore him. ﴿But if they return﴾ to fighting, ﴿then the way of the former peoples has already passed﴾, by God's granting victory to His messengers and to those who believed over those who disbelieved.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 39:

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ meaning disbelief, ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ meaning there will be no disbelief alongside your religion in the Arabian Peninsula. ﴿But if they cease﴾ from shirk, ﴿then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ He will recompense them with the recompense of One who sees them and their deeds.

[Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 40:]

﴿And if they turn away﴾: they refuse to abandon polytheism and fighting Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Then know that Allah is your Protector﴾: your Helper, O assembly of believers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 41:

﴿And know that whatever you acquire of spoils, from the unbelievers, by force, ﴿then to Allah belongs its fifth﴾. This is an embellishment at the opening of the speech, and the disposal of the fifth is directed to where thanks is due, which is His saying: ﴿and to the Messenger﴾. He had a fifth of the fifth, to dispose of as he wished; today it is spent on the welfare of the Muslims. ﴿And to the near relatives﴾, who are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, to whom the obligatory charities are forbidden, have a fifth of the fifth of the spoils. ﴿And the orphans﴾, who are the children of the Muslims whose fathers have died; they are provided for from the fifth of the fifth. ﴿And the needy﴾, who are the Muslims in need and want, also have a fifth of the fifth. ﴿And the wayfarer﴾, the one cut off from his journey, [receives from it]. So the fifth of the spoils is divided into five parts, as God Most High mentioned, and four parts of it belong to those who fought for the spoils. His saying: ﴿if you have believed in Allah﴾, that is: then do what you were commanded regarding the spoils, if you have believed in Allah ﴿and what We sent down upon Our servant﴾, meaning: this surah, ﴿on the day of the criterion﴾, the day by which He distinguished between truth and falsehood, ﴿the day the two hosts met﴾, the party of Allah and the party of Satan, ﴿and Allah is over all things competent﴾, since Allah granted you victory while you were few and humbled.

﴿When you were on the near side of the valley﴾: descending at the edge of the nearer valley, toward Madinah, while your enemy was descending at the edge of the farther valley, toward Makkah. ﴿And the caravan﴾: Abu Sufyan and his companions, who were the camel-owners, meaning the caravan (al-'Ir) ﴿was below you﴾: toward the coast of the sea. ﴿Had you arranged a meeting﴾ for battle ﴿you would have differed about the appointment﴾: you would have delayed and broken the appointment, because of their numbers and your fewness. ﴿But﴾ God gathered you without an appointment ﴿that God might accomplish a matter which was to be done﴾: in His knowledge and decree, the victory of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿That whoever perished might perish by clear evidence and whoever lived might live by clear evidence﴾: meaning, He did that so that whoever went astray and disbelieved after a proof had been established against him and his excuse cut off, and whoever believed would believe upon the same. By "clear evidence" he meant the victory of the believers, despite their fewness, over that large host despite their numbers and strength. ﴿And indeed God is All-Hearing﴾ of your supplication ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of your intentions.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 43:

﴿When Allah shows them to you in your dream as few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed about the matter, but Allah saved you. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ "In your dream" means your eye, and it is the place of sleep. "As few" so that you would belittle them and become bold against them. "And if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage" means you would have become cowardly and held back from fighting them. "And you would have disputed about the matter" means your word would have become divided. "But Allah saved you" means He protected you and spared you from opposition among yourselves. "Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts" means He knows what is in your hearts of certainty. Then He addressed all the believers with this meaning, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 44:

﴿And [remember] when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and made you few in their eyes, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done.﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: "They were made to appear few in our eyes on the Day of Badr, until I said to a man beside me: 'Do you think they are seventy?' He said: 'I think they are a hundred.' Then we took a man prisoner and asked him, 'How many were you?' He said: 'A thousand.'" ﴿And He made you few in their eyes⦆ so that they would be emboldened against you and would not turn back from fighting you. ﴿So that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾ in His knowledge, [namely] the victory of Islam and its people and the humiliation of polytheism and its people. ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾ and after this your return is to Me, so I will honor My allies and punish My enemies.

O you who believe, when you encounter a company (fi'ah), that is, a group of disbelievers, ﴿then stand firm﴾ for fighting them and do not flee, ﴿and remember God much﴾, that is, call upon Him for victory over them, ﴿so that you may prosper﴾, that is, so that you may be happy and remain in Paradise, for these are two outcomes: either booty (ghanimah) or martyrdom (shahadah).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 46:

﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart﴾: "do not dispute" means do not differ, "lest you lose courage" means become cowardly, "and your strength depart" means your vigor (jalad), your boldness, and your dominion (dawlah).

﴿Do not be like those who went out from their homes﴾, meaning: the army (al-Nafir), ﴿insolent and boastful﴾, meaning: arrogant in blessings, displaying the good while concealing the ugly, ﴿and who bar from the way of God﴾, by hostility toward the believers and fighting them. ﴿And God is encompassing of what they do﴾, meaning: He is knowing, and will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 48:

﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them﴾ — the verse. The occasion of its revelation: when Quraysh gathered for the march, they feared Kinanah and the Banu Mudlij because of past grievances between them. Iblis appeared to them in his host, in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Kinani, then al-Mudlaji. They said to him: "We intend to fight this man, and we fear your people." He said to them: "I am your protector (jar) against my people," meaning: a guardian against my people, "so no one among the people will overcome you today." ﴿And when the two hosts came in sight of each other﴾ — the two companies met. ﴿He turned on his heels﴾ — he returned, fleeing. It was said to him: "O Suraqah, are you fleeing without any fighting?" He said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾. That is because he saw Gabriel with the angels, who had come to aid the believers. ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾ — lest He destroy me along with those who are destroyed. ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 49:

﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say﴾ They are a people who embraced Islam in Makkah but did not emigrate. When the Quraysh set out to fight the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they went out with them, saying: "We will be with the larger of the two groups." But when they saw the small number of the Muslims, they said: ﴿Their religion has deluded these people﴾, for they went out, despite their small number, to fight a great host. Then they were all killed alongside the polytheists. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever puts his trust in Allah﴾, that is, entrusts his affair to Allah, ﴿then indeed Allah is Mighty﴾, strong and impregnable, ﴿Wise﴾ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 50:

﴿And if you could see﴾ O Muhammad ﴿when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved﴾, taking their spirits, meaning: those who were killed at Badr, ﴿striking their faces and their backs﴾, their fronts when they advance upon the Muslims and their rears when they turn their backs, ﴿"Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ That is: they will say to them after death: taste, after death, ﴿the punishment of the burning.﴾

"That" means: this punishment, ﴿because of what your hands have sent forward﴾, because of what you have earned and committed, ﴿and that Allah is not unjust to the servants﴾, because He judges in what He decrees.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 52:

﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾ (the verse). He means: the custom of these people in denial is like the custom of the people of Pharaoh, so God, exalted is He, sent down His punishment upon them just as He sent it down upon the people of Pharaoh. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong﴾, capable, nothing overcomes Him, ﴿and severe in punishment﴾ toward whoever disbelieves in Him and denies His messengers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 53:

﴿That is because Allah﴾ and the rest of the verse. Allah the Exalted fed the people of Makkah after hunger, gave them security after fear, and sent Muhammad (ﷺ) to them as a Messenger. All of this was among the blessings with which He favored them, and He would not have changed it for them had they not changed themselves. Their change was their disbelief in it and their neglect of giving thanks for it. So when they changed that, Allah changed what was upon them: He stripped them of the blessing and seized them. Then it was revealed concerning the Jews of Banu Qurayza:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 56:

﴿The ones with whom you made a covenant from among them﴾ (the verse). This was because they broke the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they aided the polytheists of Makkah against him with weapons. Then they made excuses and said: "We erred." So he (ﷺ) made a covenant with them a second time, and they broke the covenant on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq). This is His saying: ﴿Then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear Allah﴾. The punishment of Allah for that...

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 57:

﴿If you gain the upper hand over them in war﴾: that is, if you overtake them in fighting and take them captive. ﴿then scatter, by means of them, those behind them﴾: that is, do to them something of punishment and chastisement by which you disperse the gathering of everyone who breaks a covenant, so that they take warning from what you did to these people and do not break the covenant. This is the meaning of His the Exalted's saying: ﴿so that they may take heed﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 58:

﴿And if you fear from a people treachery﴾ you know from a people ﴿treachery﴾, meaning breaking of the covenant, by a sign that appears to you, ﴿then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms﴾. That is: throw back to them their covenant that you made with them, so that you and they are equal in enmity, and they do not suppose that you have broken the covenant by declaring war. That is: inform them that you have broken their covenant, lest they suppose you guilty of betrayal. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾, those who betray in covenants and other than them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 59:

﴿Let not those who disbelieve suppose that they have outstripped (Us).﴾ This was because those among the disbelievers who escaped from the battle of Badr feared that a destruction would befall them at that time. When it did not befall them, they became insolent and transgressed. So Allah said: Do not suppose that they have outstripped Us now by their safety; ﴿indeed, they cannot escape Us⦄ (i.e., they cannot outpace Us), nor will they elude Us in whatever times they encounter in the future.

"Prepare against them"—that is, take up the means of war against your enemy—﴿whatever force you can muster﴾, by which you may strengthen yourselves for fighting them, such as weapons, bows and other things, ﴿and horses stationed for war﴾, horses that are tethered for the sake of Allah, ﴿by which you may strike terror into the enemy of Allah and your enemy﴾, that is, the polytheists of Makkah and the disbelieving Arabs, ﴿and others besides them﴾, namely the hypocrites, ﴿whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾, because they are among you, saying, "There is no god but Allah," and they fight alongside you, and the hypocrite is troubled by the number of the Muslims. ﴿Whatever you spend in the way of Allah﴾, whether equipment and weapons, or gold and silver, in obedience to Allah, ﴿will be repaid to you﴾, meaning He will replace it for you in this world and fully recompense you for it in the Hereafter, ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾, that is, your reward will not be diminished.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 61:

﴿And if they incline to peace﴾ means they lean toward reconciliation. ﴿Then incline to it﴾ means then lean toward it. He means the polytheists and the Jews. Then this was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God﴾. ﴿And rely upon God﴾ means trust in Him. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ of what you say, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what is in your hearts.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 8, verse 62:**

﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ by means of the peace, so that you will refrain from them, ﴿then indeed, God is sufficient for you﴾, that is: the one who takes charge of your sufficiency is God. ﴿It is He who supported you﴾, strengthened you ﴿with His help﴾ on the day of Badr, ﴿and with the believers﴾, meaning: the Ansar.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 63:**

﴿And He joined their hearts together⦆ — between the hearts of al-Aws and al-Khazraj, who are the Ansar (the Helpers).

﴿Even if you had spent all that is on the earth, you could not have joined their hearts together⦆ — because of the enmity that existed between them.

﴿But Allah joined them together⦆ — because their hearts are in His hand; He joins them as He wills.

﴿Indeed, He is Almighty⦆ — nothing can elude Him.

﴿Wise⦆ — knowing what He does.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 64:

﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you﴾ (the verse). Thirty-three men and six women embraced Islam along with the Prophet (ﷺ), and then ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) embraced Islam, and this verse was revealed. The meaning: Allah suffices you, and suffices the believers who follow you.

O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. ﴿Urge them﴾ means: encourage them to support the religion of God. ﴿If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ meaning: one man among you against ten of them in battle. ﴿And if there are a hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand﴾ That is: they are in ignorance, so they will not stand firm when you fight them, unlike one who fights with insight, hoping for the reward of God. The ruling on this was for a time when one Muslim had to endure against ten of the disbelievers. So they humbly complained to God, the Mighty and Majestic, of their weakness, and then it was revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 66:

﴿Now Allah has lightened your burden﴾, He made it easy for you. ﴿And He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you a hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand﴾. So one man among the Muslims became equal to two men of the disbelievers. And His saying ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by His will that this be so.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 67:

It was revealed concerning the ransoming of the captives of Badr, who were ransomed for four thousand (dirhams) apiece. Allah, mighty and majestic, rebuked His Prophet ﷺ for this by saying: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he inflicts a massacre upon the land.﴾ That is, it was not for a prophet to hold a disbelieving captive whom he had power over for ransom. Nor is it permissible for him to do so until he thoroughly subdues (yuthkhin) in the land, that is, he exhausts himself in killing his enemies. ﴿You desire the goods of this world⦆ — that is, the ransom — ﴿but Allah desires the Hereafter⦆ — He desires for you the Garden by slaying them.

This verse clarifies what must be avoided: taking captives for favour (mann) or ransom before subduing the land by killing the enemies. This occurred on the day of Badr, and they had not yet subdued the enemy, so Allah rebuked them for it. Then there was revealed after it: ﴿Then either grant them favour afterwards or accept ransom﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 68:

﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already preceded﴾ — O Muhammad, that the spoils of war and the ransom of captives are lawful to you and to your community — ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you took﴾ — from the ransom — ﴿a great punishment.﴾ So when this was revealed, they withheld their hands from what they had taken of the spoils. Then it was revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 69:

﴿So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good; and fear Allah﴾ by obeying Him. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ He forgave you for what you took of the ransom, ﴿Merciful﴾ He showed you mercy because you are His allies.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 70:

﴿O Prophet, say to those prisoners who are in your hands: If Allah knows any good in your hearts,﴾ meaning, a desire for Islam, ﴿He will give you better than what has been taken from you﴾ meaning, of the ransom. That is: if you embrace Islam and Allah knows the Islam of your hearts, He will replace for you something better than what was taken from you. ﴿And forgive you﴾ what came from your disbelief and your fighting against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 71:

﴿And if they intend treachery against you﴾. This was because they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We believe in you and we testify that you are the Messenger of God." So God the Exalted said: if they betray you, and their saying this is treachery, ﴿then they have betrayed God before﴾, by disbelieving in Him, ﴿so He gave you power over them﴾, meaning the believers at Badr. This is a threat to them if they return to fighting. ﴿And God is Knowing﴾ of the treachery if they commit it, ﴿Wise﴾ in His management and in His recompense of them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 72:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated﴾ — the verse was revealed concerning inheritance. In the early period of Islam, they used to inherit from one another on the basis of emigration (hijrah) and support (nusrah). So a man would accept Islam but not emigrate, and therefore he would not inherit from his brother. This is His saying: ﴿those who believed and emigrated﴾, meaning they forsook (hajaru) their people, their homes and their wealth; ﴿and those who gave shelter and helped﴾, meaning the Ansar, who housed the Emigrants (muhajirun) in their homes and supported them; ﴿those are allies of one another﴾, meaning: these are the ones who inherit from one another.

﴿As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of protection toward them at all﴾, meaning: they are not allies, and inheritance is not established between you and them ﴿until they emigrate. And if they seek your help in religion﴾, meaning: those who have not emigrated, do not abandon them and support them ﴿except﴾ if they seek your help ﴿against a people between you and whom there is a covenant﴾, meaning a pact, so do not betray them nor assist them against it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 73:

﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others.﴾ That is: there is no inheritance between you and them, and no guardianship (wilayah); the disbeliever is the ally of the disbeliever, not of the Muslim. ﴿Unless you do it,⁠﴾ that is, unless you cooperate and support one another and apply in inheritance what I have commanded you. ﴿there will be fitnah (trial, discord) in the land﴾ meaning shirk (polytheism). ﴿and great corruption.﴾ That is because when a Muslim abandons his disbelieving relative, that is more likely to draw him to Islam; but if he does not abandon him and inherits from him, the disbeliever remains in his disbelief.

And His saying: ﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and strove in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped them — these are the true believers.﴾ That is: they are the ones who realized their faith through what it requires of emigration and support, unlike those who remained in the abode of polytheism.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 8, verse 75:

﴿And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and strove with you - they are of you.﴾ Meaning: those who emigrated after al-Hudaybiyah, which is the second emigration (al-hijrah al-thaniyah). ﴿And relatives are more entitled to one another﴾ Allah abrogated (naskh) inheritance through emigration and the alliance (al-hilf) after the conquest of Makkah. Allah returned the inheritances to the relatives (dhawu al-arham): the son of the brother, the paternal uncle, and others. ﴿In the Book of Allah﴾ in the judgment of Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾
